claim: AI is used mainly for research; delegated buying is small
basis: Every survey that separates research from purchase; OpenAI wound down Instant Checkout in March 2026

claim: Delegation starts with groceries and replenishment not identity purchases
basis: Consistent ranking across Gartner Accenture DOSS Checkout.com and Bain

claim: Agents show position bias and description sensitivity and injection vulnerability
basis: ACES ABxLab Magentic Marketplace and a 272000-attempt injection competition

claim: Agents are more price-sensitive than humans
basis: ABxLab human baseline 9 points not significant; models 15 to 34 points

claim: Agents are more persuadable than humans by evidence-shaped cues
basis: Best seller badges and fabricated clinical claims shift agent choice 10 to 99 points

claim: Agents verify claims and expose mediocre products
basis: Fabricated claims work; 39% of failed GPT-5 shopping runs cite unverified attributes

claim: AI recommendations are volatile run to run and across model versions
basis: SparkToro 2961 runs; replicated by Malthouse et al. and Uberti-Bona Marin et al.; ACES model-version reshuffles

claim: Brands mentioned more on the web get recommended more
basis: Correlational only; strong for Google AI Overviews weak for ChatGPT

claim: Big brands are the default for unbranded prompts
basis: One controlled study; no data on how often prompts name a brand

claim: Structured data beats editorial content
basis: Feeds gate eligibility; editorial drives the pick; Google says no special schema needed

claim: AI platforms sell ads beside answers
basis: OpenAI Google and Amazon Rufus all live

claim: Paying changes the organic recommendation
basis: None disclosed; all platforms deny; sponsored tags lower agent selection in ACES

claim: Platforms take a transaction cut
basis: OpenAI 4% fee tried January 2026 and retracted March 2026; others at zero

claim: Bot defenses block legitimate agents by accident
basis: 200-retailer audit 28 refusals all via WAF; Walmart admitted accidental blocks

claim: Retailers deliberately block agents
basis: Amazon Williams-Sonoma Kohl's Delta United Yelp

claim: The access fight is platform versus platform over the customer relationship
basis: Amazon blocks Muse while running Buy for Me on other retailers' sites

claim: Cloud-hosted agents are legally more exposed than on-device ones
basis: Ninth Circuit reasoning plus Amazon's amended complaint; untested on Muse

claim: Cancellation friction is a large share of subscription revenue
basis: Einav Klopack and Mahoney NBER: friction roughly doubles revenue

claim: Agents are eroding subscription revenue today
basis: Market reaction only; no churn data from any company

claim: Agents re-shop every reorder and erode loyalty
basis: Shipped reorder agents default to past purchases; lab agents take the first acceptable offer 60 to 100% of the time

claim: Companies are unprepared for agent intermediation
basis: HFS/Cognizant 37% have a plan; Deloitte 1 in 5 prepared; Mirakl 4.4/10

claim: Nobody owns agent experience internally
basis: Inferred from readiness data; no survey measures ownership

claim: Hidden B2B pricing is penalized by agents
basis: No study found

claim: AI-generated reviews are a growing share
basis: Platform takedowns confirm the direction; magnitudes depend on the detector

claim: Reviews are increasingly written by agents
basis: No data at all

claim: Purchase delegation could grow nonlinearly
basis: Muse downloads linear at about 230000 a day; no delegation data published
